key_insight: AUTOPILOT-VQA introduces an incident-focused benchmark to test whether vision-language models can understand safety-critical moments in dashcam videos, not just general scenes. It shifts evaluation from broad recognition to reasoning about what happened, why it matters, and what an autonomous system should infer.
problem_solved: Current vision-language and multimodal models are often evaluated on generic driving or scene-understanding tasks, but these do not reliably reveal whether they can reason about dangerous incidents in real-world dashcam footage. This paper addresses the lack of a benchmark centered on incident-centric visual question answering for autonomous driving safety.
method: Create AUTOPILOT-VQA, a benchmark built around dashcam video clips with questions focused on incident understanding.
Frame evaluation as visual question answering so models must infer event context, causality, and safety relevance from video.
Use the benchmark to compare how well vision-language models handle safety-critical driving scenarios.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more realistic way to measure whether multimodal models are trustworthy in autonomous driving settings. It helps identify model weaknesses in incident reasoning, which is essential for safety evaluation and deployment.

paper_title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
paper_authors: Siddharth Damodharan, Radhika Gupta, Ali Alshami, Ryan Rabinowitz, Jugal Kalita
